sentence: This project studies how the lateral line system of blind cavefish evolved to help catch prey, using electrophysiology and genetic analysis.
This project explores cybersecurity in modern resilient systems and turns the research into modules for classrooms.
This project maps and samples the inside of a volcano to find out how rising magma interacts with ocean crust and seafloor sediments.
This project builds computer methods that combine tensor representations with artificial intelligence to recover information from incomplete, noisy or corrupted observations.
This project works to scale up a ceramic material that can be reshaped by thermoforming after firing, so large parts can be made.
This project maps invasive Caribbean pine and burn scars with drone and satellite imagery, then forecasts pine spread and fire risk.
This project studies how a choanoflagellate and its internal microbiome adapt to extreme conditions such as high salinity, arsenic, and cyanide.
This project studies how tightly confined interfaces inside ceramic composites affect their strength and how they fail under extreme conditions.
This project tries to find out why sand lance embryos are so sensitive to ocean warming and acidification, and which genes and enzymes are responsible.
This project studies how a protein complex that protects the genome manages branched DNA structures during DNA repair.
This project develops mathematical tools that store high-dimensional information in compact form and use random projections to extract answers more efficiently.
This project tries to find out whether a protein in urine can serve as a nutrient source for bacteria that live in the bladder.
This project tests whether social wasps that live in the same habitat evolved to differ in body color to reduce competition.
This project uses satellite data and physics-informed neural networks to estimate river depth and discharge.
This project builds a unified model that maps wildfire risk and simulates how failures spread across power, water, and transportation systems.
This project tests how mitochondria in high-altitude waterbirds have changed to cope with hypoxia, including their efficiency and antioxidant defenses.
This project builds small, flexible probes that can study multiple regions of the spinal cord at the same time.
This project uses four decades of reef monitoring to find out why depleted coral populations fail to recover.
This project studies the geometry behind persistent homology, a tool that measures the shape of high-dimensional data.
